title: End of month budget review: what to check
dek: Compare consistent balance snapshots, confirm bills, and carry unpaid commitments forward. Finish with one specific change for next month.
metaDescription: Compare consistent balance snapshots, confirm bills, and carry unpaid commitments forward. Finish with one specific change for next month.

paragraphs: At month end, compare like-for-like balances, confirm which bills were paid, check unfamiliar transactions, and list commitments the next month must still cover. Finish with one concrete adjustment. A short review can reveal priorities, but it is not a substitute for resolving an error, overdue payment, or missing record.

The aim is not to grade the month. It is to make the next starting point more accurate. A higher checking balance can mean progress, or simply that a large bill has not left yet. Read the balances alongside the obligations.

body.heading: Close the period in order
items: Choose a review date and use the same account scope as the prior snapshot.
Record bank, savings, cash, and card balances with the timestamp.
Note pending items and unpaid bills that affect the comparison.
Confirm expected payments cleared and investigate discrepancies.
Review unfamiliar charges and changed recurring costs.
List next month's non-monthly bills and dates.
Carry forward outstanding obligations, not just recurring templates.
Choose one specific change and who will make it.

body.heading: Invented example: a limited snapshot
rows: Not applicable: change is measured across the period

body.heading: Explain the measure before interpreting it
paragraphs: The included cash rose by $270 and the included cards fell by $120, giving a $390 increase in this limited measure. It is not full net worth if loans, other assets, or liabilities are excluded. It is not safe-to-spend money if some of the cash is reserved or a bill remains unpaid.

Use the same accounts and a comparable point in the payment cycle each time where possible. A card payment posted on one side of the snapshot and not the other can distort interpretation. If the timing is different, write that down instead of drawing a confident conclusion from the change alone.

body.heading: Reconcile the facts that matter
paragraphs: For each expected bill, distinguish scheduled, sent, cleared, and confirmed paid. A payment screenshot may not show the biller's final status. Check outstanding items rather than automatically labeling everything green when it disappears from a task list.

For an unfamiliar charge, verify it through your statements and the provider's known contact route. Do not wait until next month's review to report a suspected error. Keep relevant records and ask the bank or issuer about the applicable process and timing.

body.heading: Carry obligations across the boundary
paragraphs: An unpaid one-off bill does not vanish because the month closed. A pending card payment, reimbursement you have not received, or expense incurred on credit also needs a place in the next plan. Mark whether it is already reflected in the opening balance to avoid subtracting it twice.

Recurring items can be copied as a starting template, then checked for new amounts and dates. A renewal, school cost, or insurance premium may be due next month even though it was absent this month. Use [sinking funds](/guides/sinking-funds-explained) for predictable future costs where feasible.

body.heading: Two lines that turn review into action

items.line: The change that helped was [specific action]. We will keep it because [observable result].
Before [date], [person] will [specific action] so that [bill or spending problem] is addressed.
We still need to confirm [payment or charge]. The owner is [person], and the next check is [date].

body.heading: Do not turn carryover into fresh income
paragraphs: Money already in an account belongs in the next opening balance, not again as new income. A transfer between your own accounts is not a second salary. If savings is protected for a known purpose, keep that purpose visible when you carry the balance forward.

Decide how to handle a surplus only after checking commitments and reserves. If spending exceeded the plan, identify the cause: an estimate was low, income changed, a one-off cost arose, or a decision changed. Each suggests a different adjustment.

body.heading: Review together without requiring universal access
paragraphs: For shared finances, compare the agreed shared scope and assign follow-up tasks. Adults can keep personal information private while sharing the facts needed to fund shared commitments. Do not assume one person's checking balance represents the whole household position.

If essentials are unpaid, there is suspected fraud, or a debt issue is worsening, stop the routine review and address that specific problem promptly. If you lack the prior snapshot, save this month's as the baseline. Inventing a starting balance adds false precision rather than insight.

items.q: How long should the review take?
items.a: A small set of accurate records may allow a brief review, but there is no guaranteed ten-minute limit. An unexplained charge, missed bill, or reconciliation issue deserves the time it needs. Keep optional analysis separate so it does not delay necessary follow-up.

items.q: Do I need every transaction categorized?
items.a: Not to make a useful first review of balances, bills, and upcoming commitments. More detail is helpful when it answers a particular question or meets a recordkeeping requirement. Missing categories should not prevent you from checking a consequential unpaid bill.

items.q: What if I have no start-of-month balances?
items.a: Use today's verified balances as your first snapshot, noting the accounts and timing included. Review bills and upcoming commitments now; begin the numerical comparison next time. Do not reconstruct an exact starting figure from memory just to complete a table.

worksheet.title: Month-end balances and carryover review
worksheet.prompt: Close one period using consistent facts and identify the next period's outstanding work.

research.intent: Close a budgeting period accurately without mistaking a partial balance snapshot for wealth or available spending.
limitations: Practical organization suggestions are not individualized professional advice.
